SettingsIntroPage.title: About this site
SettingsIntroPage.purposeIntro: This site visualizes hiking records, serving both as a personal achievement log and a platform for sharing with others. Its main features:
SettingsIntroPage.purposeItem1: Add, browse, edit, and delete hiking trails (requires login)
SettingsIntroPage.purposeItem2: User login system to protect data ownership
SettingsIntroPage.purposeItem3: Achievement dashboard showing personal activity totals
SettingsIntroPage.purposeItem5: Mobile-friendly and installable as a PWA
SettingsIntroPage.purposeNote: The design was initially inspired by Spotify's single-page feel. It was later split into a multi-page structure for clearer navigation, alongside a simulated multi-user flow.
SettingsIntroPage.techBackend: Backend & database: NestJS + PostgreSQL (hosted on Neon)
SettingsIntroPage.techVisual: Visual design: icons, logo, and hero banner all custom-drawn
SettingsIntroPage.techNote: The logo is inspired by the hiking phrase "one more bend and you're at the summit," symbolizing steady progress toward a goal. The overall color scheme and interaction flow draw inspiration from Spotify, YouTube, and Hevy.
SettingsIntroPage.problemIntro: I've long kept a habit of recording my hiking trails, but existing tools make producing, organizing, and presenting this data inconvenient:
SettingsIntroPage.problemMethodsIntro: Common ways to record a trail:
SettingsIntroPage.problemMethod1: Draw a line on Openrouteservice Maps and export as GPX
SettingsIntroPage.problemMethod2: Record a GPS track while hiking and export as GPX
SettingsIntroPage.problemMethod3: Draw the trail manually with GIS software like QGIS or ArcGIS
SettingsIntroPage.problemPainIntro: But presenting this data brought its own problems:
SettingsIntroPage.problemPain1: QGIS-exported static images aren't interactive — others can't pan or zoom them
SettingsIntroPage.problemPain2: Google Maps works for display but has limited layers, forcing all trails into one file and full rewrites on every update
SettingsIntroPage.problemPain3: Lacks flexibility and extensibility for further chart analysis or multi-user sharing
SettingsIntroPage.problemConclusion: So I extended this need into a full web app, simulating an open platform that supports multi-user uploads, interactive queries, and achievement visualization.
